title: Hruday exact finite-graph first- and second-order Wilson coefficients on the two-plaquette graph (a different finite model)
selection_reason: The Z^3 remainder constant K_2 is an upper bound; a computable finite model shows what first- and second-order coefficients actually are in a truncated graph, as a labelled comparison, never a transfer.
model: FG(two-plaquette graph of Round11: two adjacent squares sharing one link, seven links, six Gauss constraints; polynomial-degree cutoff D in {6,8} with certified tail; coupling tau_FG in a declared grid; I1.5 sign convention; gauge-invariant sector). model_is_finite_graph:true; transfers_to_aq:false.

parameters.observable: <W> of one square and its derivative at tau_FG=0 (must reproduce the matched first-order value under the graph's own normalization); second-order coefficient; the graph's own free reference computed in the same code path
parameters.admission: exact rational linear algebra (Fractions) with Ritz plus residual/Davis-Kahan or exact shell residual; python-flint Arb as labelled cross-check only
parameters.normalization_dictionary: tau_FG=tau/24 (every face coefficient nu=alpha*tau/24 in the Z^3 model; the two-plaquette graph's own coupling multiplies one face); finite-graph first-order value 1/6 <-> 1/144; consistency only
parameters.cutoff: D in {6, 8}: D is the total polynomial degree of the gauge-invariant trace-monomial basis of the Round11 solver (dimension C(D+3,3): 84 at D=6, 165 at D=8); D=6 is the primary cutoff and D=8 the certified refinement; the certified tail uses the solver's tail_lower bound (45 at D=6, 69 at D=8) together with the itemized residual ledger; no per-link spin label j_max is well-posed for this basis (modern lens update-4)
parameters.runtime_note: assistant-4 timing: about 60 s per grid point at D=8 in exact arithmetic (about 8x faster at D=6); the full grid at both signs and both cutoffs is about 8 minutes; D=10 is not declared

required: 1. Define the graph (Round11 two-plaquette: two adjacent squares sharing one link, seven links, six Gauss constraints), the gauge-invariant basis, the cutoff (declared in parameters) and the certified tail as a complete residual ledger itemizing separately: (a) the per-link representation tail beyond the cutoff for each of the seven links; (b) the joint product-channel residual across all seven links together (not implied by (a)); (c) the residual from projecting onto the six-Gauss-constraint gauge-invariant subspace; (d) the Ritz/eigenvector residual (Davis-Kahan or exact shell residual); (e) the arithmetic term (directed rounding). One nonzero omitted matrix element proves leakage; it does not bound the omitted norm from above.
2. Compute exact enclosures of <W>(tau_FG) at the declared grid points and the derivative at tau_FG=0, with the graph's own free reference computed in the same code path (own_free_reference).

3. Compare the first-order coefficient with the matched Z^3 value 1/144 under the explicit normalization dictionary tau_FG=tau/24 (the finite-graph value 1/6 corresponds to 1/144): consistency on a different finite model, never a prediction, confirmation or transfer.
4. Report second-order coefficients as finite-model values at the declared cutoffs, with the tail residual bounding the truncation error.

5. Labels and controls: finite_graph_model_id, complete_residual_all_channels, complete_residual_ledger_itemized, certified_representation_tail, own_free_reference, no_transfer_to_aq, fg_coefficients_not_fitted, sign_convention_fixture; python-flint Arb cross-check as a labelled preview only; the mandatory sentence template in the report; gate fields exported (transfers_to_aq false, model_is_finite_graph true, fg_coefficients_fitted false); freeze; skeptic pre-comparison replay from the contract alone and post-comparison review (single_direction_independent_replay).
6. Forbidden phrasings: 'predicts', 'confirms the Z^3 value'; the finite graph is 'consistent with' the matched coefficient and nothing more.
claim_exclusions: any statement about the AQ model's shift or K_2 from the graph

preregistration.clock: s=alpha*t_E/hbar, theta=alpha*t/hbar; u=s/8 and exponent 24 forbidden in packets
claim_exclusions: free reference inside enclosure => no interaction claim
whole-sequence convergence or rate in N
relabelling a static shift as dynamical
preregistration.model_id: FG(two-plaquette, D in {6,8}, tau_FG grid, I1.5, gauge-invariant)

target.quantity: certified tail and enclosure widths reported at every grid point and both cutoffs; first-order coefficient enclosure contains 1/6
target.note: feasibility/format check on a rehearsed finite-model computation (assistant-3 and assistant-4 previews), not a blind discovery threshold; the enclosures themselves are the deliverable

preregistration.error_terms_rule: an entry may be not_applicable only with a stated reason
preregistration.mandatory_sentence_template: The finite-graph derivative of <W>_FG at tau_FG=0, under the stated normalization dictionary, is consistent with the matched Z^3 first-order coefficient 1/144; this is a consistency check on a different, finite model, not a prediction, not a confirmation of the Z^3 value, and it does not transfer to any subsequential limit of the AQ construction or resolve roadmap goal 2.

acceptance.accepted_within_scope: Enclosures with certified tails at every grid point; first-order coefficient consistent with the dictionary; labels present.
acceptance.limited: Tail certified only at the smaller cutoff D=6, or the joint product-channel residual not itemized.

stop: Investigation 10 of 10; scientific production stops after this review.
